findings.reason: the plan's only open chain item would be read as the complete remaining work, and the section the same edit added would be dispatched by no reader following the chain.
findings.text: the open followup asserts "Sections 29 and 31 are the plan's remaining implementable work" while the section declarations in the same document (plan.html:23) list s3, s32 and s33 as implementable; the two sections this review reads enter no followup, and the sentence makes their absence an affirmative claim rather than an omission

findings.reason: a repair built on the stated mechanism would limit launches rather than bound the arming wait.
findings.text: the Why says "each launch the admission service attempted started another wrapper that held the arming lock while it retried", but the base takes the arming lock in the arming caller (`_ensure_watch_producer`, reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:499-518) and holds it while it waits up to 30 s for a producer to register live, while the supervisor process it starts (dispatch_watch.py:302-330) opens no arming lock and holds nothing; the refusal therefore comes from one bounded arming wait over a crash-restarting producer, and the stated per-launch-wrapper mechanism would aim a repair at launch concurrency instead of that wait window

findings.reason: splitting the node changes what is dispatched, its effort estimate and the verdict that closes it.
findings.text: the node joins three mechanisms with three distinct causes: recording the failed start's reason in the watch log and an obligations row, keeping the registration record's liveness and lease honest, and admitting a managed launch while a producer start fails; its four-assertion done-when spans all three, so one verdict cannot close it and its gate proves none of the three alone
